title: Our history - Windau
content: # Our history. # From the beginning ... We have been writing our history since 1976: back then, our company was founded when Clemens Hilker took over the small Windau country butcher's shop in Harsewinkel, East Westphalia. Even after a move from the original headquarters in the city centre to our current plant, we remain rooted in **Harsewinkel in the heart of East Westphalia** to the present day. As a family business, **Windau is now run by the second generation**. Through continuous growth, we have developed into one of the most modern production facilities in Europe with around 350 employees. With an operating area of approx. 25,000 m2 and a production volume of approx. 20,000 metric tons annually, we achieve an annual turnover of 100 million euros (2023). Our above-average export share of 25% underlines our international activities. This makes us one of the **top 100 companies** in the German meat industry today.

title: Claas reaches half-million mark with combine harvesters
content: Claas announced it has built half a million combine harvesters since the company's founding in Harsewinkel, Germany, in 1936.

title: A Visit to Claas HQ in Harsewinkel - AgWeb
content: # A Visit to Claas HQ in Harsewinkel. ## In November a trip to Harsewinkel, Germany shows the place where Claas was founded and maintains at its worldwide headquarters today. Harsewinkel, Germany is the worldwide hub for the international farm machinery company Claas. Started by August Claas, today the company makes self-propelled combines for corn, soybeans, rice and small grains; self-propelled forage harvesters; haying equipment; and tractors. Claas has invested in new facilities in Omaha, Neb., Russia, and India with the purpose to producing machines where they will be used. The manufacturing facilities there produce self-propelled forage harvesters, Xerion machines, and combines for western Europe as well as threshing modules for other markets. It takes one day’s time to assembly a combine, and the factory produces 18 to 19 combines a day. There is a one assembly line dedicated to Jaguar forage harvesters, and there are 16 machines on the assembly at a time.
